daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Stock Performance Rankings with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, write a SQL query with window functions to: (1) Calculate the 30-day moving average for each stock's closing price using AVG() OVER a window; (2) Rank stocks by their year-to-date return using RANK() OVER ORDER BY; (3) Find the date each stock hit its 52-week high using ROW_NUMBER() OVER PARTITION BY stock_id; (4) Calculate the percentage change from previous close using LAG() function. Return a result set with stock_symbol, current_price, moving_avg_30d, ytd_rank, weeks_52_high_date, and pct_change_from_prev. Filter for top 20 performers only.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Aggregation Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Download the NSW Road Crash Data (CSV format). Build a Python script using pandas to: (1) Load the raw crash data and identify missing values, data type inconsistencies, and duplicates; (2) Clean crash date/time columns and standardise location data (remove whitespace, standardise postcode format); (3) Create new calculated columns: severity_score (based on injury_type and fatality flags), crash_hour (extracted from time), and distance_from_sydney (calculated from latitude/longitude if available); (4) Filter crashes involving motorcycles only; (5) Export cleaned dataset to a new CSV with summary statistics (total crashes, injury count, average severity by local government area). Expected output: cleaned CSV + summary report printed to console.

daily_quests.title: AIHW Health Expenditure Trend Analysis: SQL + Python ETL
daily_quests.description: End-to-end data engineering task: (1) Download AIHW health expenditure data (by state, year, and health category). (2) Write Python script to: load CSV, clean column names, handle missing values, and load data into a SQLite database table named 'health_expenditure'. (3) Write a SQL query using CTEs and window functions to: calculate year-on-year expenditure growth by state using LAG(), identify the top 3 health categories by total spend per state using RANK(), and flag states where expenditure exceeded the national average using window functions. (4) Export SQL results back to pandas DataFrame, create a pivot table showing expenditure by state×category, and generate a PNG visualisation (bar chart) of growth rates by state. Expected outputs: populated SQLite DB, cleaned CSV, pivot table CSV, and growth_rates.png chart.
